penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Each Squarespace fix is a bespoke per-customer debugging task. Even with Claude doing the CSS diagnosis, a human must review, test in the live site context, and iterate — this is not automatable end-to-end at the per-ticket level.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Non-technical customers will need back-and-forth clarification on what 'fixed' looks like, screenshot sharing, and follow-up iterations — ongoing human judgement support load.

rationale: The buyer is identifiable — a paying Squarespace small business owner whose revenue form is broken — and they demonstrably pay for website tools and have tried multiple AI platforms without success, confirming real unmet demand. The fatal flaw is operational autonomy: every fix is a unique CSS/platform debugging task that requires per-customer human iteration (screenshot intake, live-site testing, back-and-forth on what 'done' looks like). Claude can assist significantly but cannot fully automate delivery for arbitrary Squarespace layout problems. This is a consulting/done-for-you service disguised as a product, which the factory cannot run hands-off. The penalties correctly sink the score below validate.
solution_plan: This opportunity does not clear the autonomy bar for autonomous factory operation. The closest viable shape would be a fixed-menu 'Squarespace CSS Fix' service (e.g. a Typeform intake + Claude prompt that generates a code snippet + a Loom-style walkthrough) — but even then, each ticket needs a human to verify the fix works in the customer's live site before delivery. A non-technical solo operator would personally become the support queue. The honest path: this is a good freelance gig, not a scalable micro-service. Drop from the factory pipeline; consider instead as a validated niche for a human-operated micro-agency outside this system.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 5, floor is 7). Total of 3.3 is also well below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Drop. The per-customer bespoke nature of CSS debugging is the structural blocker.
